title: Billing, payments and receivables
summary: Turns approved time and disbursements into signed Ontario accounts with HST, collects payment by card, EFT or trust application, allocates every dollar, and chases what is owed. The agent drafts the bills, checks them, matches payments and writes reminders. A lawyer approves each bill, write-off, credit note and trust application before it takes effect.

Entries on a matter covered by an ethical wall must not appear to walled users
Two lawyers on one matter: only the responsible lawyer can close the review
screens.reg: RPC 3.6-1: a fee must be fair and reasonable and disclosed in a timely way. Charging for time not spent, or billing clerical work as legal work, is a fee complaint risk. Notify the client when fees are about to exceed an estimate (RPC 3.6 commentary, verify).

screens.agent: Renders the bill, computes HST and totals, runs the pre-flight checklist (registration number present, address complete, fee agreement terms match, trust proposal does not exceed the client's trust balance, no lines older than the retainer date, totals reconcile with pre-bill), and drafts the cover email.
screens.gate: G-B2: responsible lawyer approves and signs the final bill. Nothing is numbered or sent before this.
edge: HST registration missing in firm settings: block approval
Client in another province or outside Canada: agent flags place-of-supply question, lawyer picks the rate
Bill total zero after write-offs: allow a no-charge bill for the record
Bill numbering collision after concurrent approvals: number assigned in a single transaction
discount requested after approval: only via credit note (deliberate; Clio optionally allows editing approved bills)
partial payment then discount: allocation order fees > disbursements > interest made explicit on the bill
Quebec client: GST and QST shown as two lines, QST rate 9.975% (verify with Revenu Quebec)
BC, Manitoba or Saskatchewan client: PST on legal services per that province's rules (verify per province)

place of supply changed after approval: an approved bill is immutable and never returns to draft. Before delivery: void it (keeps its number, exact reversal) and approve a new bill; after delivery: full credit note and a new bill (BIL-C-207, BIL-C-084)
screens.reg: Solicitors Act s.2: no action to recover fees until one month after a bill signed by the lawyer (or accompanied by a signed letter) is delivered; delivery by hand, mail or at the client's office or residence (verify electronic delivery practice). Excise Tax Act invoice information: supplier name, registration number, date, amount paid or payable, tax charged (rules vary by invoice amount, verify). RPC 3.6: fees and disbursements shown separately (verify). Out-of-Ontario clients: GST plus provincial PST/QST, or another province's HST, per the Excise Tax Act place-of-supply rules (verify).

actions.note: G-B4; executed by the trust area's transfer flow

screens.gate: G-B4: a lawyer authorizes each withdrawal of trust money for fees. No agent action moves money.
edge: Deposit not yet cleared
Client instructed in writing not to use trust for fees
Money held for a specific purpose
Bill later reduced by credit note after transfer: excess must go back to trust
Partial transfer leaves a fee balance in AR
screens.reg: BL9: money may be withdrawn from trust for fees only for services already performed and only after a bill has been delivered to the client; no client ledger may go into overdraft; electronic transfers need the authorization and record set out in BL9 (verify all section numbers). Cross-ref trust area.

screens.agent: Pulls payments from the provider adapter and bank feed, matches by bill number, amount, payer and memo, posts exact matches if policy allows, flags overpayments, unknown payers and fee money that landed in trust or retainer money that landed in operating.
screens.gate: G-B3: a clerk or lawyer confirms ambiguous allocations and anything involving trust.
edge: Overpayment: held as unapplied client credit for at most N business days (firm setting, default 5; verify against By-Law 9), then applied to a delivered bill of the same client with client direction (G-B3), refunded (G-B6) or paid into trust (G6); an exception is raised at N days. Never moved silently, never to another client
Chargeback or NSF: reverse allocation and reopen the bill
Cash at or above the BL9 cash limit: refuse and alert the lawyer
Payment for a matter the clerk is walled from
Duplicate webhook from the provider
screens.reg: BL9: cash received on one client file aggregating $7,500 or more is refused, counting trust and operating (fee) cash together, unless an exception is recorded (G6c; ss.4-6, verify); processor fees and chargebacks may not be paid out of trust (verify); retainer money must be deposited to trust. BL7.1: verification of identity when funds move (verify trigger).

fields.note: 1998BI only: currency code, tax rate, tax type

actions.name: Record rejection and reopen
actions.note: reopen means credit note + re-bill

screens.agent: Validates codes, totals and tax lines; maps rejection reasons back to lines.
screens.gate: none to export; correcting a rejected bill goes through credit note (G-B5) and new bill.
edge: client rejects for block billing: agent splits narratives on re-bill
time or expense lines missing UTBMS codes: export refused with the list of lines
download does not mark the bill as sent; sending is a separate step

screens.name: Payment plans and autopay
screens.purpose: Let a client pay a balance in instalments, or pay bills automatically from a stored card or bank account.
screens.layout: List of plans with next charge; detail shows schedule, consent record, history of charges and failures.

fields.name: Frequency
fields.note: weekly | every 2 weeks | monthly

fields.name: Stored method
fields.note: tokenized by processor; never stored by us

fields.name: Autopay new bills
fields.note: charge each new approved bill on its due date

fields.name: Client authorization
fields.note: pre-authorized debit agreement or card-on-file consent

fields.name: Destination
fields.note: operating only; a plan never pays into trust unless set up as a trust request

fields.name: Autopay trigger
fields.note: on approval | on due date | N days after delivery; never before the account is delivered; per client under G-B9

screens.agent: Sends reminders before each charge, retries once on failure, alerts lawyer after second failure.
screens.gate: Lawyer approves plan terms; client authorizes in portal.
edge: card expires mid-plan
new bill raises the balance: plan not changed without consent
client revokes PAD authorization
screens.reg: Pre-authorized debits follow Payments Canada Rule H1 (notice and cancellation rights) (verify).

screens.name: Online payment settings
screens.purpose: Connect the payment processor, map payouts to real bank accounts, and set methods, fees and surcharge rules.
screens.layout: Processor connection card; accounts mapping; methods; fees and surcharge; receipt template.

fields.name: Fee source
fields.note: processor fees always charged to operating, never to trust

fields.name: Methods
fields.note: card, debit, Interac e-Transfer, EFT/PAD (bank debit is our addition: Clio Payments Canada documents cards and Apple/Google Pay only)

fields.name: Card surcharge
fields.note: off by default; credit cards only; never on debit, prepaid, digital wallets or trust payments; blocked for a Quebec firm or a card with a Quebec billing address

fields.name: Surcharge rate
fields.note: capped at the lower of 2.4% and the firm's cost of acceptance; shown as its own line with the percent

fields.name: Surcharge notice date
fields.note: card-network notice filed 30 days before surcharging starts (Mastercard form by firm; Visa notice via processor)

fields.name: Surcharge-free method offered
fields.note: required true before surcharge can be enabled

fields.name: PAD agreement on file
fields.note: per payer; Payments Canada Rule H1 agreement and waiting period; PAD into trust needs an agreement naming the trust account

fields.name: Fee schedule
fields.note: daily | monthly: when processor fees are debited

fields.name: Primary operating account
fields.note: debited for processing fees, chargebacks and shortfalls; never a trust account

fields.name: Statement descriptor
fields.note: 5-22 Latin characters the client sees on the card statement

fields.name: Processor data region
fields.note: where payer data is processed; prefer Canada and show it in the privacy notice

actions.name: Change deposit accounts
actions.note: trust account mapping change needs a licensee sign-off

actions.name: Enable surcharge
actions.note: blocked until notice date passed, surcharge-free method on, and agent's law society rule check attached

screens.agent: Watches for fees debited from trust or chargebacks against trust and raises a trust exception. Before surcharge is enabled, checks the province's law society position and the card-network notice date and attaches the result.
screens.gate: Licensee signs off any change to where payments land.
edge: chargeback on a card payment already in trust: shortage risk, trust exception
refund to card after trust funds were spent
card with a Quebec billing address at checkout: surcharge line removed before charge
client pays a surcharged bill with a debit card: no surcharge
payment toward a retainer request (trust): surcharge never applied; on a bill payment the surcharge carries HST at the bill's tax codes (BIL-T-044, verify)
processor reports a chargeback on a trust deposit: shortfall debited from primary operating account, trust ledger untouched, exception raised
screens.reg: Trust deposits must arrive in full; processor fees must not be taken from trust (BL9, verify). Canadian card surcharging (per the processor's published Canada rules): credit cards only, capped at the lower of 2.4% and cost of acceptance, not on debit, prepaid, wallets or trust payments, not for Quebec firms or Quebec cardholders, 30-day network notice, and a surcharge-free payment option must be offered. Whether the LSO permits passing card fees to clients on fee accounts is a separate check (verify).

agent_jobs.does: Recomputes aging and interest, sends friendly reminders under template, drafts firm notices

agent_jobs.does: Matches provider payouts and fees to posted payments; checks no fee hit trust

agent_jobs.name: Monthly billing digest
agent_jobs.does: WIP, billed, collected, realization, AR over 60, HST by period

agent_jobs.output: interest line on next bill or statement for G-B2

open_questions: Which payment provider(s) first, and do we hold separate merchant accounts for trust and operating per firm?
May the agent auto-send approved bills and auto-post exact-match payments, or must a human click each one?
Is electronic delivery (portal or email) enough for Solicitors Act delivery at our firms, or should the bill always also carry a signed cover letter? (verify with counsel)
Write-off threshold that needs the managing lawyer's second approval.
Do we support LEDES / insurer e-billing in v1, or only PDF bills?
Do we charge interest on overdue accounts by default, and at what rate? It must be in the retainer.
Out-of-province and non-resident clients: do we compute the HST/GST place of supply ourselves or let the lawyer choose the rate?
Is QuickBooks/Xero export needed in v1 for operating-side accounting?
Do we allow card surcharging at all in v1?
LEDES export in v1, or later when an insurer-client firm signs up?
Combined bills across a client's matters: allowed, given trust is per matter?
Could: early-payment discount % and valid days on payment profiles, removed by the agent on expiry, pre-tax?
Could: when a draft bill line is edited, update the source time entry by default before approval?
Could: SMS bill reminders with amount and pay link only, with per-contact consent?
Could: let a firm override payment plan allocation (default oldest due bill first)?
Could: live preview with a sample bill on bill-themes (no drag-and-drop designer in v1)?
Could: show 'approved by / at' on bills and on the versus page as a difference from Clio?
Could: operating-account payment link/QR with no amount, landing in payments-inbox as 'needs client'?
Could: autocharge a stored card on an approved retainer request (trust) with a consent record?
Could: consumer financing (Pay Later) - would LSO accept financed funds into trust?
Could: require a processor that keeps Canadian payer data in Canada?
sources: https://lawsociety.mb.ca/?p=4670 (comparable rule: bill before trust withdrawal)
